text:
Sam: FYI merged main -> feature/optimize-batching earlier and the post-merge nightly smoke on h100 just went red :disappointed:
Sam: CI output shows warmup OOM on shard 7, looks like memory footprint jumped after this PR
ci-bot: build #4287 failed on shard=7 job=nightly-h100-warmup test=smoke (OOM) -- logs: https://ci.internal/r/4287
Nina: ugh, thanks for flagging. can you paste the exact OOM trace?
Sam: sure, copying snippet from the log:
```
[2024-06-24 03:12:33] ERROR: c10::CUDAException: CUDA out of memory. tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 80.00 GiB total capacity; 72.10 GiB already allocated; 1.90 GiB free; 72.15 GiB reserved)
Backtrace:
  File "/opt/workspace/runner/infer/runtime.cc", line 412, in allocate_kv_cache
  File "/opt/workspace/runner/warmup/runner.cc", line 128, in warmup_sequence
```
Nina: that reserve/allocated numbers look suspicious (72G reserved). the PR touched batching code, maybe prefix caching retention changed.
Ryan: did the PR change default batch_size or kv cache retention? I skimmed it but didnt dive in.
Sam: changed default continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 4096 and added a per-request kv_keep flag (defaults to true).
Devon: maybe increasing max tokens makes warmup hold larger caches across tokens. could blow past the per-shard allowance on h100.
Nina: can we repro locally on a h100 canary or smaller image? If it's a config regression maybe we can run smoke with `--max-batch-tokens=2048` to confirm.
Sam: repro steps I used:
1) checkout feature/optimize-batching
2) docker build -t rwinf:bbox . (uses ubuntu+cuda 12.2 + driver 535.86)
3) run: `./scripts/ci_smoke.sh --device h100 --shard 7 --warmup-seqs=8`
I hit OOM consistently.
Ryan: quick triage idea: revert the default in config to 2048 in the canary config and rerun nightly, see if that fixes. If yes, it's config-aware not allocator bug.
ci-bot: triggered rerun #4288 (canary with config override) by @Ryan
Devon: I'll bisect the PR range tomorrow morning if the config revert doesn't help. leaving notes here so oncall knows.
Sam: thanks. also noticed `nvidia-smi` during warmup shows all processes accumulating persistent allocations (not freed between sequences). snippet:
```
# nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
pid, used_memory [MiB]
1234, 73240
1235, 128
1236, 512
```
Sam: that process 1234 is the runner. seems to reserve big chunk and keeps it.
Nina: possible causes: kernel-level allocation change, or we keep multiple kv caches pinned. try forcing `KV_CACHE_MODE=release_on_sequence_end` env var (non-default) to see if memory drops.
Sam: good call. I'll rerun with `KV_CACHE_MODE=release_on_sequence_end` and `--max-batch-tokens=2048` -> warmup completed successfully on the canary image (no OOM).
Nina: ok that narrows it. sounds like interaction between raising max_batch_tokens and default kv retention.
Ryan: action items: (1) Sam open a hotfix PR to set default max_batch_tokens back to 2048 and kv_keep=false for canary; (2) Devon bisect PR range to find the change in cache lifecycle; (3) add a lightweight smoke that checks warmup mem on h100.
Sam: created hotfix PR #4290 with the config reversion and tests pinned. pinging reviewers.
Devon: starting bisect, will post progress. if I find the offending commit I'll file a targeted revert or patch.
ci-bot: hotfix PR #4290 triggered premerge pipeline by @Sam
Sam: thanks everyone. I'll monitor nightly next run and loop back once bisect results are in. :thumbsup:
